::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 9th 1879  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54921: 97-98
:::

Dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd)

Here is the list of materials for [the little Christmas book](cmy_books/cmybook_135.qmd).

The MS, and the clipping come herewith the four others must be sent by rail in the books in which they appeared.[^1] The Autobiography of Patty Applecheeks came out in an American paper, and my copy of it has been lost, but I am sending to Philadelphia to see whether I can recover it. The Wedding cake (a story of a ridiculous mistake) I also sent to America, and was paid for it, but it has never appeared and I am writing to beg that it may. Both these are of the length  of the Phantom

If a little more were needed, I could write one more. There are two stories, one called <u>the Banks of the Leamy</u>, which [Warne](people/person_1433.qmd) bought for a Christmas annual, and [Sea Spleenwort](cmy_books/cmybook_46.qmd), which [Groombridge](organizations/other_148.qmd) had, which it is a pity not to recover and unite with the rest, but I cannot afford  to advance anything to buy back the copy rights.

What an excellent life of [Burns](other_books/otherbook_919.qmd) Principal Sharp’s is.  He has some qualities (Sharp I mean superior to any writer of the day. I am much tempted to write an answer to the Rights of Woman paper, but I don’t know if [Mr Grove](people/person_588.qmd) would accept my view of the question, and defence of the poor mothers and chaperons[^1]

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: She was assembling previously published stories which appeared as *Bye-Words* (1880).

**Note:** Perhaps Florence W. Habberton, ‘Individual Liberty for Women: A Remonstrance’, *Macmillan's Magazine* 40 (1879), 282-288.  George Grove was the editor of *Macmillan’s*.
